portName: Honolulu Harbor (Pier 2 and Pier 11, Aloha Tower)
language: English (Hawaiian is also an official language)
seoTitle: Honolulu cruise port guide: Pearl Harbor and Diamond Head
seoDescription: Ships use Pier 2 or Pier 11 by Aloha Tower. Waikiki 15 min by car. Arizona Memorial free but book on Recreation.gov ($1). Diamond Head $5, reservation only.
quickAnswer: Most ships dock at Pier 2 on Ala Moana Boulevard; a second ship uses Pier 11 by Aloha Tower, about half a mile away, close to downtown and Chinatown. Downtown is walkable, but Waikiki is about 15 minutes by car and Pearl Harbor about 9.5 miles away, so use a taxi, ride-hail or TheBus ($3.25 a ride from July 2026). Book the USS Arizona Memorial and Diamond Head before you sail, and leave Pearl Harbor two hours before all-aboard.
intro: Honolulu Harbor puts you on the edge of downtown, within walking distance of Chinatown and the Aloha Tower, with Waikiki a short drive east along the shore. The day here is shaped by reservations rather than distance: the USS Arizona Memorial programme, Diamond Head and ʻIolani Palace all need tickets booked in advance, and walk-up entry is either limited or not offered. Pick one booked anchor for the day, build the rest around it, and allow for Honolulu traffic on the way back.

terminals.name: Pier 2 Cruise Terminal
terminals.notes: The primary cruise terminal, used by most lines, at 521 Ala Moana Blvd; the entrance is at the west end of Channel Street. Kakaʻako is just under a mile away. Follow current signs for the ground-transport area, which the state has changed. No wi-fi at the terminal.

terminals.name: Pier 11 (Aloha Tower)
terminals.notes: The alternate terminal, used when a second ship is in. Entrance on the north extension of Aloha Tower Drive, beside Aloha Tower Marketplace, a couple of blocks from Chinatown. Free wi-fi at the marketplace.

walkability.detail: Downtown and Chinatown are walkable from Pier 11; the King Kamehameha I statue downtown is about 15 minutes on foot from the port. Waikiki (hotels about 3.3–4.8 miles away), Pearl Harbor and Diamond Head need transport.

transportSections.cost: $3.25 cash per boarding, exact fare, no transfers; $7.50 daily cap with a HOLO card ($2 card fee) (from July 2026)
transportSections.time: Pearl Harbor from Waikiki about 1 hour or more
transportSections.detail: Route 20 runs between the airport and stops near both piers (Ala Moana Blvd opposite South St for Pier 2; S. King St and Bethel St for Pier 11). For Pearl Harbor from Waikiki, the W Line and Route 42 board on Kuhio Avenue. Drivers carry no change. A HOLO card gives transfers and the daily cap; buy or load it at holocard.net or a HOLO retailer.

transportSections.cost: Waikiki to Pearl Harbor: Uber about $26–41, taxi $45–70 (2026)
transportSections.time: About 15 min to Waikiki; 25–30 min to Pearl Harbor without traffic
transportSections.detail: The most practical option for a timed Pearl Harbor or Diamond Head slot. Rush hour runs towards Honolulu from about 06:00 to 08:30 and out to the west from about 15:30 to 18:30.

transportSections.time: About 15 min to the King Kamehameha I statue
transportSections.detail: From Pier 11 you can walk to Chinatown and downtown. From Pier 2 allow longer; the piers are about half a mile apart.

returnTiming.rule: Be back on board 60 minutes before all-aboard. Leave Pearl Harbor two hours before all-aboard by taxi or ride-hail, Waikiki or Diamond Head 90 minutes before, and downtown 75 minutes before.
returnTiming.detail: Pearl Harbor is 25–30 minutes away in light traffic, but the afternoon rush starts around 15:30. Diamond Head entry slots also run to a fixed timetable, so a late slot leaves little room.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Order a ride-hail rather than waiting for a bus. If you will miss all-aboard, call the port agent number on your daily programme straight away.

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: Free programme plus $1 Recreation.gov fee; ride-hail or TheBus there and back (2026)
diyVsExcursion.saving: Large, if you secure a reservation

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: $5 entry per non-resident, plus taxi or bus (2026)

excursionAdvice: If you could not get USS Arizona Memorial tickets on Recreation.gov, a ship's Pearl Harbor tour is the most reliable way in, because same-day in-person tickets are no longer issued and standby waits can last hours. The same applies to Diamond Head if the 30-day window sold out before you booked. Otherwise downtown, Chinatown, ʻIolani Palace and Waikiki are easy on your own with a ride-hail.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at 07:00, all-aboard is 17:30, a weekday from Tuesday to Saturday, and a USS Arizona Memorial reservation for about 09:30.

steps.what: Ride-hail from the pier to the Pearl Harbor Visitor Center. Leave all bags on the ship; only a small wallet is allowed.
Arrive at least an hour before your programme. Check in at the Ticket Validation Desk 10 minutes before your time.
USS Arizona Memorial programme: orientation, boat to the memorial and back. Watch the 23-minute film and the free museums before or after.
Lunch in Chinatown, for example a poke bowl at Maguro Brothers.
ʻIolani Palace tour (booked in advance; 60–90 minutes), at King and Richards Streets.
Walk back past the Aloha Tower to the pier.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Pearl Harbor National Memorial and USS Arizona Memorial
sights.why: The site of the 7 December 1941 attack; the programme takes you by boat to the memorial over the sunken battleship.
sights.cost: Free; $1 Recreation.gov fee per ticket; parking $7 (2026)
sights.tip: Tickets open at 15:00 HST 8 weeks ahead, with more released at 15:00 the day before. No bags larger than a small wallet; paid bag storage is near the entrance. Visitor centre open 07:00–17:00, programmes 08:00–15:30.

sights.name: Diamond Head State Monument
sights.why: The crater trail climbs to the rim for views over Waikiki and the coast.
sights.tip: Non-residents must book on gostateparks.hawaii.gov, up to 30 days ahead; people without a reservation are turned away. Arrive within the first 30 minutes of your slot. Last reservation 16:00; everyone must be out by 18:00.

sights.name: ʻIolani Palace
sights.why: The palace of Hawaii's last monarchs, in downtown Honolulu.
sights.tip: Open Tuesday to Saturday 09:00–16:00, closed Sunday and Monday. Tickets are online only: no walk-ups or same-day bookings. No large bags, backpacks, food or drink inside.

sights.name: Waikiki
sights.why: Honolulu's resort district and beach, about 15 minutes by car from the harbour.
sights.tip: Combine with Diamond Head: TheBus Route 23 runs from Waikiki to the crater entrance.

sights.name: Chinatown
sights.why: A couple of blocks from Pier 11, with an arts district and some of the city's best-known restaurants.
sights.tip: Easy to fit in at the end of the day if your ship is at Pier 11.

sights.name: Aloha Tower
sights.why: Opened in 1926 and for four decades the tallest building in the islands; it still marks the cruise piers.
sights.tip: The state lists the tower as closed indefinitely, so do not plan on going up.

sights.name: Kakaʻako and SALT at Our Kakaʻako
sights.why: A district of shops and cafés just under a mile from Pier 2.
sights.tip: The nearest food and coffee stop if your ship is at Pier 2.

beaches.name: Waikiki Beach
beaches.note: Honolulu's main resort beach; the stretch in front of the Hilton Hawaiian Village is Kahanamoku Beach.

beaches.name: Ala Moana Beach
beaches.time: About 10 min by car (Ala Moana area)
beaches.note: Next to Kakaʻako and Ala Moana Center, closer to the piers than Waikiki.

beaches.name: Hanauma Bay
beaches.note: Tickets open 48 hours ahead at 07:00 HST. Open Wednesday to Sunday 06:45–16:00, no entry after 13:30. Tight on a cruise day.

commonMistakes.mistake: Turning up at Pearl Harbor without a USS Arizona Memorial reservation.
commonMistakes.fix: Book on Recreation.gov 8 weeks ahead or at 15:00 HST the day before. Same-day in-person tickets are no longer issued.

commonMistakes.mistake: Taking a bag to Pearl Harbor.
commonMistakes.fix: Leave it on the ship. Only a small wallet is allowed; storage costs extra and adds a queue.

commonMistakes.mistake: Going to Diamond Head without a reservation.
commonMistakes.fix: Non-residents need an advance slot from gostateparks.hawaii.gov; you will be turned away otherwise.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning ʻIolani Palace on a Sunday or Monday, or as a walk-up.
commonMistakes.fix: It opens Tuesday to Saturday only and sells tickets online in advance.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming you dock at the same pier as last time.
commonMistakes.fix: Check whether your ship is at Pier 2 or Pier 11; they are half a mile apart and directions differ.

safety: Honolulu is generally safe for visitors. Use normal city awareness in downtown and Chinatown, especially after dark. The real risks on a port day are heat and sun on the Diamond Head trail and ocean conditions at unguarded beaches; swim where lifeguards are on duty. Keep valuables out of sight in parked or hired cars.
accessibility: Pier 2 has porters and luggage storage, but wheelchair services and accessible ramps or lifts are not listed. At Pearl Harbor, ask the park (808 422-3399) about access on the memorial boat. The Diamond Head trail climbs 560 feet over 1.6 miles round trip and is not suitable for wheelchairs. ʻIolani Palace tours cover two floors; ask the palace about access when booking. Ride-hail drivers can drop you close to most downtown sights.
rainyDay: Pearl Harbor's museums, ʻIolani Palace and Ala Moana Center work in rain. Diamond Head's trail is exposed; if it is wet, use your slot only if you are confident on slippery steps.
crowdTips: Pearl Harbor programmes run every 15 minutes from 08:00; booking a morning slot leaves the afternoon free and keeps you clear of the late traffic. Book Diamond Head as soon as the 30-day window opens for your date. Avoid the westbound afternoon rush from about 15:30 if you are heading back from Pearl Harbor late.

faqs.q: Where do cruise ships dock in Honolulu?
faqs.a: Most use Pier 2 at 521 Ala Moana Blvd. A second ship uses Pier 11 beside Aloha Tower, about half a mile away.

faqs.q: Is Honolulu walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Partly. Downtown and Chinatown are walkable, especially from Pier 11. Waikiki, Pearl Harbor and Diamond Head need a car or bus.

faqs.q: How do I get from Honolulu cruise port to Waikiki?
faqs.a: A taxi or ride-hail takes about 15 minutes. TheBus costs $3.25 a ride from July 2026, exact cash or HOLO card.

faqs.q: Do I need tickets for Pearl Harbor?
faqs.a: The USS Arizona Memorial programme is free but needs a Recreation.gov reservation ($1 fee). Tickets open 8 weeks ahead and at 15:00 HST the day before.

faqs.q: Do I need a reservation for Diamond Head?
faqs.a: Yes, for non-residents. Book on gostateparks.hawaii.gov up to 30 days ahead; entry is $5 per person and parking $10.

faqs.q: Can I bring a bag to Pearl Harbor?
faqs.a: No. Only items up to the size of a small wallet are allowed. Paid storage is near the entrance.

faqs.q: What can I do in Honolulu in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Pearl Harbor in the morning, then lunch in Chinatown and ʻIolani Palace, or Diamond Head and Waikiki.
No. Ships dock at Pier 2 or Pier 11 in Honolulu Harbor.
